interactions.summary: The class detours through mirror neurons, false-belief psychology, and awkward personal examples, while Jiang stays skeptical of reductive neuroscience and keeps the problem of empathy open.
interactions.speaker_attribution: Jiang-led exchange with student anecdotes and theories

claims.claim: Jiang treats mirror neurons as a possible but unconfirmed neuroscientific explanation for empathy and openly resists treating the theory as settled fact.
Student contributions present empathy as both a developmental capacity and a socially uneven skill, illustrated through personal difficulty recognizing when tears call for shared feeling.
Jiang leaves the mechanism unresolved and thereby creates space for a later move toward empathy as something possibly irreducible to brain theory alone.

signature_moments.moment: Jiang refuses easy scientific closure and says plainly that we do not actually know how empathy works.
signature_moments.source_phrase: We don't even know how this works
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It clears the ground for the later spiritual account of empathy.

signature_moments.moment: A student tries to push empathy beyond the single mind altogether and treats it as intrinsically divine.
signature_moments.why_it_matters: This gives Jiang the opening he wants for the spark theory in the next packet.

glossary_terms.definition_or_usage: Mirror neurons appear here as a proposed but doubted neuroscientific mechanism for empathy.

chronology_notes.note: The catharsis discussion passes through scientific and psychological hypotheses but ends by reopening empathy as a deeper metaphysical question.

uncertainty_notes.note: The student description of the developmental experiment is halting and imprecise, so it should be treated as classroom evidence of a line of thought rather than as a reliable summary of the underlying study.
